name: krakenkey-api
description: Tools for interacting with the KrakenKey TLS certificate management and endpoint monitoring API

auth.description: User API key (kk_...) or JWT access token. Probe routes also accept a service key (kk_svc_...)

tools.name: get_api_status
tools.description: Check that the KrakenKey API is running and get its version

tools.name: liveness_check
tools.description: Liveness check. Returns 200 whenever the API process is serving requests; does not check dependencies

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Readiness check covering the database, Redis, and the Authentik auth provider. Returns 503 when any of them is down

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Get the authenticated user's profile, plan, org membership, and resource counts. Resource counts are pooled across all members when the user belongs to an organization

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Update the authenticated user's display name or email notification preferences. Preference keys are merged into the existing settings; omitted keys keep their current value (unset keys default to enabled). Returns the full profile

tools.name: confirm_auto_renewal
tools.description: Confirm the user still wants automatic renewal. On the free plan, auto-renewal pauses when the last confirmation is more than 6 months old; this resets the confirmation timestamp. Paid plans are not affected

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: List the API keys created by the authenticated user, newest first (metadata only, never the secret)

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Create a new user API key. The key value (kk_...) is returned only once; store it immediately. Returns 402 when the plan's API key limit (pooled across org members) is reached

expiresAt.description: Expiry timestamp. Omit for a key that never expires

tools.name: delete_api_key
tools.description: Delete one of the authenticated user's API keys. Returns 404 if the key does not exist or belongs to someone else

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: List domains registered by the authenticated user, or by any member of the user's organization

tools.name: register_domain
tools.description: Register a domain for certificate issuance. Returns a verificationCode that must be published as a DNS TXT record on the hostname itself. If the caller already registered this hostname, the existing record is returned. Returns 402 when the plan's domain limit (pooled across org members) is reached

hostname.description: Fully qualified domain name (e.g., example.com). Verifying a domain also authorizes all of its subdomains

response.verificationCode: string (publish as a TXT record at the hostname)

tools.name: get_domain
tools.description: Get one domain owned by the caller or a member of the caller's organization
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_domains item)

tools.name: verify_domain
tools.description: Look up the hostname's DNS TXT records and mark the domain verified if one contains the verificationCode. Returns the domain immediately if it is already verified. Returns 400 if the record is missing or the DNS lookup fails. This only checks the TXT record; the _acme-challenge CNAME is checked later, when a certificate is issued
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_domains item, with isVerified: true)

tools.name: delete_domain
tools.description: Delete a domain. Returns an empty body on success

tools.name: list_certificates
tools.description: List TLS certificates owned by the authenticated user, or by any member of the user's organization

response.status: string (pending | issuing | issued | failed | renewing | revoking | revoked)
response.failureReason: string (why the last attempt failed) | null

tools.name: submit_csr
tools.description: Submit a PEM-encoded CSR for issuance. Keys must be RSA >= 2048 bits or ECDSA P-256/P-384. Every name in the CSR must be a verified domain or a subdomain of one (wildcards allowed), and each name needs an _acme-challenge CNAME delegated to KrakenKey or issuance fails. Issuance is async; poll get_certificate. Resubmitting the same CSR within 15 minutes returns the original certificate instead of a new one (409 while the original request is still being created). Returns 402 when a certificate plan limit is reached

csrPem.description: PEM-encoded CSR (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----...-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----)

response.status: string (pending, or the current status on an idempotent replay)

tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description: Get a certificate and its status. When status is 'issued', crtPem holds the leaf certificate and chainPem the intermediates. crtPem and chainPem are null while a renewal is running and after a failure
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_certificates item)

tools.name: get_certificate_details
tools.description: Get parsed details of the leaf certificate. Returns 400 if the certificate has no PEM yet (not issued)

tools.name: get_certificate_chain
tools.description: Get the leaf details, parsed intermediates, and a ready-to-deploy full chain PEM (leaf followed by intermediates). Use fullChainPem for nginx, Caddy, HAProxy and similar servers. For intermediates only, use chainPem from get_certificate. Returns 400 if the certificate has no PEM yet

tools.name: update_certificate
tools.description: Toggle automatic renewal for a certificate. Returns the updated certificate
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_certificates item)

tools.name: renew_certificate
tools.description: Renew an issued certificate using its original CSR. Only works when status is 'issued'. Subject to the same plan limits as issuance (402). Async; poll get_certificate until status returns to 'issued'. crtPem and chainPem are cleared while the renewal runs, so save the current certificate first if you still need it

tools.name: retry_certificate
tools.description: Re-queue issuance of a failed certificate using its original CSR. Only works when status is 'failed'. Subject to the same plan limits as issuance (402). Fix the cause first (for example a missing _acme-challenge CNAME), since permanent failures repeat

tools.name: revoke_certificate
tools.description: Revoke an issued certificate with the CA. Only works when status is 'issued' and only on certificates the caller created (not other org members'). Synchronous: returns status 'revoked' on success; on a CA error returns 500 and the status goes back to 'issued'

tools.name: delete_certificate
tools.description: Delete a certificate record. Only works when status is 'failed' or 'revoked' (400 otherwise)

tools.name: list_endpoints
tools.description: List monitored endpoints owned by the authenticated user or their organization, newest first, with hosted regions and connected probe assignments

tools.name: create_endpoint
tools.description: Register a host:port for TLS monitoring and request an immediate scan. If the caller already has an endpoint with the same host and port, that endpoint is updated (label, sni, extra probes and regions merged) and returned. Returns 403 when the plan's monitored endpoint limit is reached; hosted regions are subject to the add_hosted_region limits
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_endpoints item)

tools.name: get_endpoint
tools.description: Get one monitored endpoint with its hosted regions and probe assignments
tools.response: object (same shape as a list_endpoints item)

tools.name: update_endpoint
tools.description: Update an endpoint. Host and port cannot be changed. probeIds and hostedRegions, when provided, replace the existing assignments entirely

isActive.description: Inactive endpoints are not handed to probes

tools.response: object (same shape as a list_endpoints item)

tools.name: delete_endpoint
tools.description: Delete a monitored endpoint. Hosted regions and probe assignments are deleted with it; existing scan results are kept but unlinked from the endpoint. Returns an empty body

tools.name: request_endpoint_scan
tools.description: Ask probes to scan this endpoint now. Probes that fetch their config within the next 5 minutes see scanNow: true for it. Results show up in get_endpoint_latest_results once a probe reports

tools.name: list_my_probes
tools.description: List connected (self-hosted) probes registered by the authenticated user or their organization, most recently seen first. Use these IDs with assign_probes

tools.name: assign_probes
tools.description: Assign connected probes to an endpoint. A connected probe only scans endpoints assigned to it. IDs that are not connected probes owned by the caller or their organization are skipped silently; already-assigned probes are left as is

tools.name: unassign_probe
tools.description: Remove a connected probe from an endpoint. Returns 404 if the probe is not assigned. Returns an empty body

tools.name: add_hosted_region
tools.description: Have KrakenKey-operated probes in a region scan this endpoint. Not available on the free plan. Returns 403 when the plan has no hosted monitoring, or when the hosted endpoint or hosted region limit (pooled across org members) is reached. Adding a region the endpoint already has returns the existing record

region.description: Region identifier (e.g., us-east-1). Must match the region a hosted probe registers with

tools.name: remove_hosted_region
tools.description: Remove a hosted probe region from an endpoint. Returns 404 if the endpoint does not have that region. Returns an empty body

tools.name: get_endpoint_results
tools.description: Get paginated scan results for an endpoint, newest first (ordered by scannedAt). Results older than the plan's retention period are deleted daily

tools.name: get_endpoint_latest_results
tools.description: Get the most recent scan result from each probe that has scanned this endpoint. Useful for current status across all probes
response: object (same shape as a get_endpoint_results data item)

tools.name: export_endpoint_results
tools.description: Download all stored scan results for an endpoint as a file attachment (not paginated), newest first. JSON is an array of scan result objects; CSV has one row per result

tools.name: register_probe
tools.description: Register a probe, or heartbeat an existing one (same probeId). Sets status to 'active' and updates lastSeenAt. With a user API key or JWT the probe is linked to that user; with a service key it is a hosted probe with no owner
tools.auth_type: dual (service key, user API key, or JWT)

region.description: Required in practice for hosted probes; used to select endpoints by hosted region

tools.name: submit_probe_report
tools.description: Submit TLS scan results from a registered probe (404 if the probeId is not registered). Each result is matched to the caller's endpoints by host and port. Use mode 'connected' with a user API key; 'hosted' is reserved for KrakenKey-operated probes using a service key, and standalone results are not stored. Results with no matching endpoint are skipped, not rejected
tools.auth_type: dual (service key, user API key, or JWT)

mode.description: 'connected' for self-hosted probes using a user API key

timestamp.description: Stored as scannedAt on every result

items.certificate: object (optional): subject, sans, issuer, serialNumber, notBefore, notAfter, daysUntilExpiry, keyType, keySize, signatureAlgorithm, fingerprint, chainDepth, chainComplete, trusted

tools.name: get_probe_config
tools.description: Fetch the endpoints a probe should scan. With a user API key or JWT (connected probe): active endpoints owned by the caller that are assigned to this probe. With a service key (hosted probe): all active endpoints that have a hosted region matching the probe's registered region. Returns 404 if the probe is not registered
tools.auth_type: dual (service key, user API key, or JWT)

endpoints.scanNow: boolean (present and true when a scan was requested in the last 5 minutes)

tools.name: public_scan
tools.description: Run an on-demand TLS scan of a public hostname. No authentication. Raw IP addresses are rejected, and hostnames that resolve to private or reserved addresses return 400. Returns 503 if the scanner is unavailable

hostname.description: DNS name (letters, digits, hyphens, dots). No IPs, ports, or wildcards

response.certificate: object (optional): subject, sans, issuer, serialNumber, notBefore, notAfter, daysUntilExpiry, keyType, keySize, signatureAlgorithm, fingerprint, chainDepth, chainComplete, trusted

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Submit product feedback with a message and a 1-5 rating

tools.name: create_organization
tools.description: Create an organization with the caller as owner. Requires a Team, Business, or Enterprise plan (402 otherwise); the owner's subscription becomes the org subscription. Returns 409 if the caller already belongs to an organization

tools.name: get_organization
tools.description: Get organization details including the member list

tools.name: update_organization
tools.description: Rename an organization. Caller must be an owner or admin of this organization. Returns 409 while the organization is being dissolved

tools.name: delete_organization
tools.description: Delete (dissolve) an organization. Owner only (403 otherwise). Dissolution runs in the background: the org is marked 'dissolving', members' domains, certificates, and API keys are transferred to the owner, members are detached, billing reverts to the owner personally, and the org is removed. Returns 204 with no body

tools.name: invite_member
tools.description: Add an existing KrakenKey user to the organization by email (they must have logged in at least once). Caller must be an owner or admin. Returns 404 if no user has that email, 409 if they are in another org or have an active, uncanceled paid subscription. Returns 201 with no body

tools.name: update_member_role
tools.description: Change a member's role. Caller must be an owner or admin. The owner's role cannot be changed here; use transfer_ownership. Returns 200 with no body

tools.name: remove_member
tools.description: Remove a member from the organization. Owners and admins can remove others; any member can remove themselves. The owner cannot be removed (400). Returns 204 with no body

tools.name: transfer_ownership
tools.description: Make another member the owner. Only the current owner can call this; they become an admin. Returns 404 if no member of this org has that email. Returns 201 with no body

email.description: Email of the member who becomes owner

tools.name: create_checkout_session
tools.description: Start a paid subscription. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for the user to open in a browser. In an organization, only the owner can manage billing (403). Returns 400 if the plan is not available for purchase

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.description: Get the current subscription (the org subscription for organization members). Users without a subscription record get a default free/active response

response.id: string (UUID, omitted on the default free response)
response.createdAt: ISO8601 (omitted on the default free response)

tools.name: create_billing_portal_session
tools.description: Get a Stripe Customer Portal URL for managing payment methods, invoices, and cancellation. Org owner only when in an organization (403). Returns 404 if the user has no subscription record

tools.name: preview_upgrade
tools.description: Preview the immediate charge for upgrading an active paid subscription to a higher plan. The charge is the flat difference between the two plan prices (no day-based proration). Returns 404 with no active paid subscription (use create_checkout_session from free), 400 if the target is not higher than the current plan

tools.name: upgrade_plan
tools.description: Upgrade an active paid subscription to a higher plan and charge the price difference immediately. Same preconditions and errors as preview_upgrade

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List all users. Admin only: the caller must be in the 'authentik Admins' group (403 otherwise)
tools.auth_type: admin (JWT or user API key, caller in the 'authentik Admins' group)
response: object (user record, same shape as get_user)

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Get a user record. Callers can read their own record; admins can read any (403 otherwise)

id.description: User ID (the Authentik subject, same as get_profile id)

tools.name: update_user
tools.description: Update fields on a user record. Callers can update their own record; admins can update any (403 otherwise). Prefer update_profile for display name and notification settings
tools.response: object (database update result, not the updated user)

tools.name: delete_user
tools.description: Permanently delete a user account. Callers can delete their own account; admins can delete any (403 otherwise). Issued certificates are revoked with the CA (reason keyCompromise, best effort), then the user's certificates, domains, and API keys are deleted and their feedback is anonymized. Cannot be undone
